slides.lead: Five steps between your toilet and the river, as Thames Water explains them.
Thames Water treats 4,600 million litres of sewage every day, at over 350 works, for 16 million customers.

steps: Screens remove wipes, nappies and cotton buds, then grit.
Settlement tanks let solids sink as sludge.
Air is pumped in so useful bacteria break down the waste.
A final tank lets the bacteria sink out. Some works also filter through sand.
Treated water goes back to local rivers and streams, regulated by the Environment Agency.

paras: Sludge is digested to make biogas, which is burned for heat and electricity.
What's left is recycled to farmland as fertiliser.
When works can't treat all the flow, the extra goes into storm tanks.
When those fill, untreated wastewater can spill into rivers or the sea.

slides.lead: Over 65,000 blockages a year in Thames Water's region come from the wrong things going down drains.

tips: Bin wipes, nappies and cotton buds.
Keep fat, oil and grease out of the sink.
